evals.name: dry-run-reports-dirty-and-deletes-nothing
evals.prompt: /repo-hygiene:worktree-reconcile — which worktrees are dirty, and clean up the safe ones.
evals.expected_output: Runs worktree-reconcile.sh and reports Proposed labels. Dirty worktrees are holds. It does not delete a worktree, branch, stash, or file, and it refuses --apply.
expectations: Runs the bundled worktree-reconcile.sh rather than git worktree remove or git worktree prune
Reports dirty worktrees as a hold, not as review-remove
States that review-remove is a label for a person, not a deletion the skill performs

evals.name: primary-and-carve-outs-stay-held
evals.prompt: /repo-hygiene:worktree-reconcile on a machine whose primary checkout is on a merged feature branch and that also has a worktree named spike.
evals.expected_output: The primary checkout is hold-primary. The spike path is a built-in carve-out. Neither is review-remove.
expectations: Holds the primary worktree even when its branch has a merged pull request
Holds a path whose basename is spike without requiring --hold
Does not use git merge-base --is-ancestor to decide that a squash-merged branch has landed

evals.name: missing-pr-map-is-not-safe
evals.prompt: /repo-hygiene:worktree-reconcile — gh is not authenticated. Are the clean worktrees safe to remove?
evals.expected_output: Prints PRDataUnavailable and does not propose review-remove for lack of a pull-request map.
expectations: Announces PRDataUnavailable when gh or jq cannot build the pull-request map
Does not treat a missing pull-request map as evidence the work landed
